Compound Wahala › Pidgin words

Naija Pidgin words & phrases

Compound Wahala is in English with Nigerian Pidgin. Here is what the Pidgin means — useful for players outside Nigeria, diaspora kids and curious grown-ups.

Words

Wahala
Trouble, stress or a big fuss. "Compound wahala" = drama in the compound.
Example: No wahala! (No problem!)
NEPA
What many Nigerians still call the electricity company. Used for the power supply itself.
Example: NEPA don take light! (The power is out!)
Don
Shows that something has happened (like "has").
Example: Light don come! (The power is back!)
Dey
Is / are / is happening.
Example: Rain dey come! (Rain is coming!)
Chop
To eat. Also food.
Example: Who chop the meat? (Who ate the meat?)
Abeg
Please.
Example: Abeg, help me find am! (Please help me find it!)
Am
Him, her or it (after a verb).
Example: I dey sell am. (I sell it.)
Na
It is / it's (points at something).
Example: Na me? (Is it me?)
Wetin
What.
Example: Wetin happen? (What happened?)
Palaver
A long argument or trouble.
Example: Fuel palaver (an argument about fuel)
Ahn ahn!
A shout of surprise or protest, like "Ah! Come on!"
Example: Ahn ahn! NEPA don take light again!
O
Added at the end of a sentence for emphasis.
Example: Me I hear drumming o!
Compound
A shared yard with several homes around it, where neighbours share a gate, water tank and often a generator.
Example: Unity Compound, 7 Adebayo Close
Owambe
A big, colourful Nigerian party (especially Yoruba celebrations).
Example: The compound looks like an owambe!
